A second reviewer found: p2: 'The following references were reviewed and incorporated into this fact sheet' - ISID 2022, Morgan 2004, PAHO 2004, PAHO/ICRC 2016. question: Is it in scope? A second reviewer found: Scope: written for detainee/dislocated-civilian camp operations under DoD control - Appendix B is JP 3-07/JP 4-02/DoDI 2310.08 doctrine, the method centres on the LADS laundry system, Appendix D lists DoD-supply NSNs; Appendix C summarises WHO/PAHO/APHA and quotes one WHO sentence. Only about one page (54 C wash, 60 C dry, bag clothing) is general-use. Release and pictures fine.

title: Aerographer's Mate Module 5: Basic Meteorology

Preface: "2001 Edition Prepared by AGC(AW/SW) RICK KROLAK", a Navy chief, "Published by Naval Education and Training Professional Development and Technology Center". The file is a Wayback Machine raw capture (15 December 2001) of the Navy's official NETPDTC address advancement.cnet.navy.mil/products/web-pdf/tramans/fullbook/14312.pdf. This answers the earlier rejection in REJECTED.md, which rested only on the militarynewbie.com copy having no second copy. SHA-256 4db1051d3b274b80decf85ec12c9415e0683b5888a996dce98078e4b5f6e0954.
evidence: DISTRIBUTION STATEMENT A: Approved for public release; distribution is unlimited. (cover, PDF page 1; repeated on PDF page 2)
creditsNote: Whole text searched and every hit read in context. Hits: the course answer-sheet boilerplate, "taken from" in physics text, two Air Weather Service (US Air Force) publications, AWS/TR-79/006 and AWS/TI-84/001, and "your local power company" in a question. Picture audit, 20 November 2026: every page with a picture (90 of 252 pages) was looked at by eye, with zooms on anything small. No picture carries a credit line, copyright notice, signature, watermark, logo or brand. Open point for the owner: Figure 6-2 (PDF page 168), a Navy redraw with figure id AG5f 0602, is titled "CLIMATIC TYPES OF THE EARTH (after Köppen)". "After" says the map is adapted from Wladimir Köppen (died 1940). His classification and maps appeared between 1900 and 1936, so whether the source is long out of copyright (the Beaufort case in ruling 2) depends on which map was followed. No other source is printed on the map (zoomed). Table 6-2, "Trewartha's Climatic Groups and their Poleward Boundaries", states a named classification's boundaries in the Navy's own typeset table with no credit line, so it is taken as a summary (a citation). Uncredited photographs: solar-disk photographs (Figure 1-2, page 14), a four-frame tornado sequence (Figure 5-6, page 147) and scanned world pressure maps (Figures 3-3A/B, page 60). Each carries a Navy figure id and no marks when zoomed, and none is stock imagery or a product photograph, so they are taken as the Navy's own. Figure 1-10 (page 29) has a small engraving-style wind-head drawing with no signature (zoomed to 500 dpi). Page 97 carries the standard US government note that international boundaries are not necessarily authoritative. Text: the 7 pages without a text layer are all blank; scrambled lines 0.02 percent (PyMuPDF) and 0.1 percent (pdftotext). No safety advice beyond mentions; page 5-11 repeats the dated idea that pressure drop makes buildings explode in a tornado, without advice.
question: Is Figure 6-2 (PDF page 168), a Navy redraw titled "CLIMATIC TYPES OF THE EARTH (after Köppen)", the Navy's own? "After" says it is adapted from Wladimir Köppen's classification (he died in 1940); no credit line or other owner is shown. Everything else is clean (see creditsNote). Yes lists it; no keeps it out.

title: Freezing Meat and Poultry Products for Home Use
licenceNote: US government work (17 U.S.C. 105); the proof rests on staff authorship. Home and Garden Bulletin No. 15 (formerly AWI-75), issued November 1951, is published under the U.S. Department of Agriculture's name and 'Prepared by Bureau of Animal Industry, Agricultural Research Administration' (cover). No personal author, outside author, photographer, illustrator, university or company is credited, there are no acknowledgements and there is no copyright notice. The document prints no public-domain statement of its own. USDA's site notice (usda.gov, Policies and Links, read 18 November 2026): 'Most information presented on the USDA Web site is considered public domain information.' The file is the National Agricultural Library's own scan, with its stamp and a handwritten '#15' on the cover. The library's old download address no longer serves it, so the address is the Wayback Machine's raw capture of that address.
evidence: Cover (PDF page 1): 'U.S. DEPARTMENT OF AGRICULTURE / Prepared by Bureau of Animal Industry / Agricultural Research Administration / Washington, D. C. / Home and Garden Bulletin No. 15 / Formerly AWI-75 / November 1951'. PDF page 2: 'This folder was prepared in the interests of food conservation for farm families and others who use frozen-food lockers or who have home freezing cabinets.' Back page: 'U. S. GOVERNMENT PRINTING OFFICE 16-39565-5'. The scan is a fold-out sheet cut into 11 page images; two headings run across page joins (7/8 and 9/10) and no text is lost. Safety, checked against today's advice: store at 0 deg F; storage months (sausage and ground meat 1-3, fresh pork and fish 3-6, lamb and veal 6-9, beef, poultry and liquid eggs 6-12) are quality limits close to current USDA charts, and food held at 0 deg F stays safe; thaw in the refrigerator and cook thawed food promptly; chill carcasses at 33 to 39 deg F; scald poultry at 128 to 140 deg F. Dated but not unsafe: when wrapping paper is short, dip frozen cuts for 5 seconds in lard heated to 200 deg F (a burn risk the folder does not mention), and its locker-plant and 1944-45 calendar context.
creditsNote: Picture audit, 20 November 2026: all 11 pages were rendered and the 7 that carry a picture (PDF pages 1, 3, 5, 7, 8, 10, 11) were looked at by eye at full size; pages 2, 4, 6 and 9 are text panels seen on a contact sheet. No picture carries a credit, a name, a signature or a maker's mark: a cover photograph of a slice of meat, line drawings of poultry, eggs and fish, carcass-cutting diagrams, photographs of meat cutting and wrapping, and an unsigned cartoon of a couple at a locker plant beside 1944 and 1945 calendars. The cover also carries the library's received stamp and a handwritten '#15'. None of the 19 embedded images carries ownership wording in its data; the only notice in the file data is the stock sRGB colour profile's own 'Copyright Hewlett Packard, 2004' tag, which belongs to the profile and not to any picture.
question: Is this dated or outdated safety advice? A second review found the pictures clean and the rest sound (0 F storage, thaw in the refrigerator, cook thawed food promptly), but PDF page 3 heads the poultry panel 'DRESS—CHILL—DRAW': chill the bird with its guts still in and draw it afterwards, with no time or temperature. Today's home-processing advice is to draw promptly and chill the carcass to 40 F within hours. Thawed raw eggs are also not limited to cooked dishes, and the page 11 lard dip at 200 F is a burn risk the folder does not mention. The reviewer leans keep. Yes lists it; no keeps it out.

PDF page 11: '... prepared by the Science and Education Administration's Federal Research staff', 'U.S. GOVERNMENT PRINTING OFFICE : 1978'. The reference list cites outside books and papers; nothing is reproduced from them. Safety: sugar syrup, candy and dry-sugar feeding and pollen-substitute recipes; it warns never to feed honey from unknown sources because it may carry American foulbrood. It says only in general terms that 'therapeutic drugs may be incorporated' in syrup; it names no drug or dose, and since 2017 US beekeepers need a veterinarian for antibiotics.

question: Is this outdated drug advice? A second review found the pictures clean, but PDF page 8 says 'All medicants that are presently recommended for the prevention or treatment of brood diseases and Nosema can be fed in protein supplement diets', and PDF pages 9-10 say 'Therapeutic drugs may be incorporated in sirup'. Today antibiotics for bees need a veterinarian (US, since 2017), preventive use is discouraged, and they are not authorised in the UK or EU. No drug or dose is named. The reviewer leans drop (Agriculture Handbook 335 was dropped partly for named bee drugs). Yes lists it; no keeps it out.
